title: “He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous” — the Greek says he lays up “salvation” for the upright
summary: In the KJV the Lord lays up sound wisdom for the righteous. In Brenton’s Greek he lays up salvation (σωτηρίαν) for those who set things right.
text: KJV Proverbs 2:7: “He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly.” Hebrew (WLC) 2:7: [וְצָפַן כ] (יִצְפֹּ֣ן ק) לַ֭יְשָׁרִים תּוּשִׁיָּ֑ה מָ֝גֵ֗ן לְהֹ֣לְכֵי תֹֽם׃. Brenton’s Greek 2:7: Καὶ θησαυρίζει τοῖς κατορθοῦσι σωτηρίαν, ὑπερασπιεῖ τὴν πορείαν αὐτῶν, [And he lays up salvation for those who set things right; he will shield their way]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/2/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO02.htm.
reasoning: The verb and the recipients line up in the two verses, but the thing laid up differs. The KJV names sound wisdom; the Hebrew word printed there is תּוּשִׁיָּה. The Greek prints σωτηρίαν, a word for salvation or safety. The Hebrew edition quoted prints no word that the Greek page repeats, so the nouns are different on the page.
scope: T applies at Proverbs 2:7 and only to the noun laid up (“sound wisdom” against “salvation”). The record does not say the KJV is wrong or that the Greek is wrong, and it does not decide how the Hebrew word should be read. Proverbs 2:8 is not compared. title: “Her paths unto the dead” — the Greek has “the earth-born” (2:18, 9:18) and “an assembly of giants” (21:16)
summary: Three Hebrew phrases use the same word, רְפָאִים. The KJV renders it “the dead” each time (2:18, 9:18, 21:16). Brenton’s Greek renders it “the earth-born” (γηγενῶν, γηγενεῖς) at 2:18 and 9:18 and “giants” (γιγάντων) at 21:16.
text: KJV Proverbs 2:18: “For her house inclineth unto death, and her paths unto the dead.” KJV Proverbs 9:18: “But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.” KJV Proverbs 21:16: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” Hebrew (WLC) 2:18: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה אֶל־מָ֣וֶת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְאֶל־רְ֝פָאִ֗ים מַעְגְּלֹתֶֽיהָ׃. Hebrew (WLC) 9:18: וְֽלֹא־יָ֭דַע כִּֽי־רְפָאִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם בְּעִמְקֵ֖י שְׁאֹ֣ול קְרֻאֶֽיהָ׃ פ. Hebrew (WLC) 21:16: אָדָ֗ם תֹּ֭ועֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃. Brenton’s Greek 2:18: Ἔθετο γὰρ παρὰ τῷ θανάτῳ τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς, καὶ παρὰ τῷ ᾅδῃ μετὰ τῶν γηγενῶν τοὺς ἄξονας αὐτῆς. [For she has set her house beside death, and her tracks beside Hades, with the earth-born]. Brenton’s Greek 9:18: Ὁ δὲ οὐκ οἶδεν ὅτι γηγενεῖς παρʼ αὐτῇ ὄλλυνται, καὶ ἐπὶ πέταυρον ᾅδου συναντᾷ· [But he does not know that earth-born ones perish beside her, and he comes upon the πέταυρον of Hades]. Brenton’s Greek 21:16: Ἀνὴρ πλανώμενος ἐξ ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης, ἐν συναγωγῇ γιγάντων ἀναπαύσεται. [A man who wanders from the way of righteousness will rest in an assembly of giants]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/2/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/9/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/21/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO02.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO09.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO21.htm.
reasoning: In the Hebrew edition quoted, 2:18, 9:18 and 21:16 each print רְפָאִים. The KJV has “the dead” at all three. The Greek page prints a different noun: “earth-born” at 2:18 and 9:18, “giants” at 21:16. The KJV and the Greek therefore name different beings at the end of the strange woman’s path and for the man who wanders from understanding.

title: “As a fool to the correction of the stocks” — the Greek has “as a dog to bonds”, and a deer struck by an arrow at 7:23
summary: In the KJV the young man follows the woman “as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks”, “till a dart strike through his liver”. Brenton’s Greek has an ox and a dog (κύων) and then a deer (ἔλαφος) struck in the liver by an arrow.
text: KJV Proverbs 7:22: “He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;” KJV Proverbs 7:23: “Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life.” Hebrew (WLC) 7:22: הֹ֤ולֵ֥ךְ אַחֲרֶ֗יהָ פִּ֫תְאֹ֥ם כְּ֭שֹׁור אֶל־טָ֣בַח יָבֹ֑וא וּ֝כְעֶ֗כֶס אֶל־מוּסַ֥ר אֱוִֽיל׃. Hebrew (WLC) 7:23: עַ֤ד יְפַלַּ֪ח חֵ֡ץ כְּֽבֵדֹ֗ו כְּמַהֵ֣ר צִפֹּ֣ור אֶל־פָּ֑ח וְלֹֽא־יָ֝דַ֗ע כִּֽי־בְנַפְשֹׁ֥ו הֽוּא׃ פ. Brenton’s Greek 7:22: Ὁ δὲ ἐπηκολούθησεν αὐτῇ κεπφωθείς· ὥσπερ δὲ βοῦς ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἄγεται, καὶ ὥσπερ κύων ἐπὶ δεσμοὺς, [And he followed her, κεπφωθείς; and as an ox is led to slaughter, and as a dog to bonds]. Brenton’s Greek 7:23: ἢ ὡς ἔλαφος τοξεύματι πεπληγὼς εἰς τὸ ἧπαρ· σπεύδει δὲ ὥσπερ ὄρνεον εἰς παγίδα, οὐκ εἰδὼς ὅτι περὶ ψυχῆς τρέχει. [or as a deer struck in the liver by an arrow; and he hurries like a bird into a snare, not knowing that he runs for his life]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/7/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO07.htm.
reasoning: At 7:22 the KJV’s second comparison is a fool; the Greek’s is a dog. At 7:23 the KJV has the dart strike the man’s liver, with the bird comparison after it; the Greek has the one struck in the liver be a deer, with the bird afterwards. title: “A prating fool shall fall” (10:10) — the Greek says “he who reproves openly makes peace”
summary: The KJV ends 10:10 with the same words it ends 10:8: “a prating fool shall fall”. Brenton’s Greek ends 10:10 differently from 10:8: “he who reproves with boldness makes peace” (εἰρηνοποιεῖ).
text: KJV Proverbs 10:10: “He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.” KJV Proverbs 10:8: “The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.” Hebrew (WLC) 10:10: קֹ֣רֵֽץ עַ֭יִן יִתֵּ֣ן עַצָּ֑בֶת וֶאֱוִ֥יל פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט׃. Hebrew (WLC) 10:8: חֲכַם־לֵ֭ב יִקַּ֣ח מִצְוֹ֑ת וֶאֱוִ֥יל פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט׃. Brenton’s Greek 10:10: Ὁ ἐννεύων ὀφθαλμοῖς μετὰ δόλου, συνάγει ἀνδράσι λύπας· ὁ δὲ ἐλέγχων μετὰ παῤῥησίας, εἰρηνοποιεῖ. [He who winks with the eyes with guile gathers griefs for men; but he who reproves openly makes peace]. Brenton’s Greek 10:8: Σοφὸς καρδίᾳ δέξεται ἐντολὰς, ὁ δὲ ἄστεγος χείλες σκολιάζων ὑποσκελισθήσεται. [The wise in heart will receive commandments, but the loose-lipped one who twists words will be tripped up]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/10/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO10.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted ends 10:8 and 10:10 with the same three words, וֶאֱוִיל פָתַיִם יִלָּבֵט, and the KJV renders both the same way. The Greek renders 10:8 with a clause about the loose-lipped being tripped up and 10:10 with a different clause about a man who reproves openly making peace. At 10:10 the KJV’s outcome is a fool falling; the Greek’s is a reprover making peace.
scope: T applies at Proverbs 10:10 and only to its second half. Proverbs 10:8 is quoted to show that the KJV and Hebrew repeat the clause and the Greek does not. title: “He that is despised, and hath a servant” — the Greek has a man in dishonour “serving himself”
